title: Rényi Diffusion Models
claim: Our method achieves the best combination of sample quality and density estimation, dominating prior methods that trade one off against the other.
layout: single scatter plot, FID on x, NLL on y, ours highlighted in red
description: A single wide scatter plot with Fréchet Inception Distance (FID, lower is better) on the x-axis from 1.5 to 15 and negative log-likelihood (NLL, lower is better) on the y-axis from about 1.5 to 4. Many baseline diffusion and flow methods (DDPM, ScoreODE, EDM, CTM, FM-OT, VDM, MuLAN, DistAug and others) appear as small dark-blue crosses, each with a blue text label next to it, scattered across the plot with no clear correlation between the two metrics. Light gray gridlines run behind the points. The proposed method, RDM (ours), is a single gray filled circle with a red outline and a bold red label. It sits in the bottom-left corner, which is the best region for both metrics. The red label against the blue crosses draws the eye there first.
caption: Perceptual quality versus density estimation performance
abstract: The choice of training objective is central to diffusion-based generative modeling in terms of both sample quality and distribution coverage. While standard maximum likelihood training provides a principled objective with strong theoretical grounding, empirical studies indicate that previous training objectives in diffusion models often face an inverse correlation between likelihood optimization and perceptual evaluations. We propose the Rényi diffusion model, a unified generative framework that formulates training objectives using Rényi divergence. This yields a generalized score matching objective providing explicit control over the trade-off between sample quality and distribution coverage. Experiments demonstrate improved balance between density estimation and sample generation performances across multiple datasets without modifying model architectures or sampling procedures.
